hook: SCP-3319 is a white dome in the Canadian Arctic, painted with a strangely tender slogan, that makes anything coming within 500 meters vanish. The file refuses to stay put: it gets revised, defaced and revised again, and much of the fun is watching the report format buckle. Keep the short notice at the very top in mind, the one about the page turning up in a database with no known origin. Expect heavy profanity and one comment describing a suicide attempt.
whyItMatters:
This is a story told through version history. Every revision shifts the object class and trims the procedures, until at one point they consist of a single dismissive word.

Its tags tie it to the Three Moons Initiative and Corbenic, and the article presents both as powers that dwarf the Foundation, yet whose internal bureaucracy turns out to be just as petty. Comment threads, a vandalised entry and a dry chronology all carry the plot in turn.
thingsToNotice:
The revisions leap ahead by decades: in 2537 containment is dropped so staff can fight SCP-001, in 2560 the dome is written off as neutralized because it fails to make SCP-001's floodwater vanish, and in 2577 everyone is advised to find a comfortable place to sleep through humanity's erasure. Then the end just stops: a satellite catches something white and oblong leaving orbit and blossoming open, and a five-point note explains that Earth now sits inside Corbenic, which is technically an afterlife, so one employee who cut his wrists simply keeps bleeding without dying.

The rescue goes sour: a panicked vandal begs people to board the dropships before something harvests them for a banquet, and a clipped timeline shows JALAKÅRA, the rescuers' own ruler, vetoing forced evacuation on grounds of formatting and procedure while the Striders take more than 43 million people for eternal digestion; just 43 are saved and hired as entry-level thralls, and Earth itself ends up as the extra moon that renames the Initiative.

The last version rewinds to the opening text, except the class is now Thaumiel and the dome carries three moons instead of two. Its addendum is addressed to Naismith, the same name as the director whose warning opens the page, and the Initiative admits it wants humans safe but watches them repeat the same mistakes, closing with a threat to step in again.
